lessons.title: Linear Seating Arrangement Basics
lessons.concept: Linear arrangement problems place people/objects in a row. Clues describe relative positions (left/right, immediate left/right, between). Draw a row of slots and place fixed or most certain information first, then use relative clues step by step.
lessons.formula: Approach: identify total positions -> fix direct clues -> apply relative clues -> check consistency with all conditions.
lessons.worked_example: If A sits to the immediate left of B in a row facing north, A and B occupy adjacent seats with A on B's left side. Place B, then put A immediately to its left.
mistakes: Confusing left and right when direction faced is not specified or changes
Not verifying the final arrangement against every clue

lessons.title: Circular Seating Arrangement Basics
lessons.concept: In circular arrangements, people sit around a table facing center or facing outward. Left/right depends on facing direction: facing center, left is clockwise and right is anticlockwise; facing outward, it reverses. Fix one person as reference to break rotational symmetry.
lessons.formula: Fix one position as reference. Facing center: left = clockwise, right = anticlockwise. Facing outward: left = anticlockwise, right = clockwise.
lessons.worked_example: Five friends face the center around a table. If B is to the immediate right of A, then moving anticlockwise from A gives B (because facing center, right is anticlockwise).
mistakes: Applying left/right without considering facing direction
Treating circular positions like a straight line at the ends
Forgetting that positions are relative around the circle (no fixed 'first' unless stated)

lessons.title: Deduction Strategies and Common Clues
lessons.concept: Common clues include immediate neighbors, 'between', 'second to the left/right', and 'not adjacent'. Use elimination and combine clues. When multiple possibilities exist, test each against all clues and discard inconsistent ones.
lessons.formula: Use strongest clues first (exact positions/immediate neighbors) -> combine with between/second-to clues -> eliminate impossible cases.
lessons.worked_example: If C is between A and B, possible orders include A, C, B or B, C, A in that block. Use other clues (e.g., A at an end) to determine the exact order.
mistakes: Assuming only one order for 'between' clues
Stopping after placing some people without satisfying all clues

practice.question: Five people A, B, C, D, E sit in a row facing north. A is at the left end. B is immediately to the right of A. Who is second from the left?
practice.explanation: Left end (1st) is A. Immediately to the right of A is B, so B is 2nd from the left.

practice.question: In a row facing north, P sits to the immediate left of Q, and R sits to the immediate right of Q. What is the order of P, Q, R from left to right?
practice.explanation: P is immediately left of Q, so P, Q. R is immediately right of Q, so Q, R. Combined order from left to right is P, Q, R.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: Four friends sit around a circular table facing the center. If B is immediately to the right of A, in which direction from A (around the table) is B located?
practice.explanation: When facing the center of a circle, a person's right side is in the anticlockwise direction around the table. So B is anticlockwise from A.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: In a row of 5 seats facing north (positions 1 to 5 from left to right), M sits at position 3. N sits immediately to the left of M. At which position is N?
practice.explanation: Immediately to the left of position 3 is position 2. Therefore N sits at position 2.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: Three people X, Y, Z sit in a row facing north. Y is between X and Z. X is at the left end. What is the order from left to right?
practice.explanation: X is at the left end. Y is between X and Z, so Y must be in the middle and Z at the right end. Order is X, Y, Z.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Four students P, Q, R, S sit in a row facing north. P is at the right end. Q is immediately to the left of P. Who is at the 3rd position from the left if the row has 4 positions total?
questions.explanation: With 4 positions from left to right (1-4), P is at position 4 (right end). Q is immediately left of P, so Q is at position 3.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: In a row facing north, A is to the immediate right of B, and C is to the immediate right of A. Which person is in the middle of these three?
questions.explanation: A is immediately right of B gives B, A. C is immediately right of A gives B, A, C. So A is in the middle.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Four people sit around a circular table facing the center. D is immediately to the left of A. In which direction from A is D located?
questions.explanation: When facing the center, a person's left side corresponds to the clockwise direction around the table. Therefore D is clockwise from A.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Five people sit in a row facing north in positions 1 to 5 from left to right. T sits at position 4. U sits immediately to the right of T. What is U's position?
questions.explanation: Immediately to the right of position 4 is position 5. So U sits at position 5.

questions.question: In a row facing north, L, M, N sit such that M is between L and N. N is at the right end of these three. What is the order from left to right?
questions.explanation: M is between L and N, so M is in the middle. N is at the right end, so L must be at the left end. Order is L, M, N.
